questions.question: Give three reasons why people trade.
questions.expected_answer: No person, community or country can produce everything it needs. Different places have different resources, such as soil, minerals or a good climate, so each place is good at producing certain things. People produce surpluses and specialise in certain kinds of work, and then trade to get what they lack.

questions.question: Explain what barter is and describe two problems with barter.
questions.expected_answer: Barter is exchanging goods or services directly for other goods or services without money. Problems are that you must find someone who has what you want and also wants what you have, that goods such as cattle are hard to divide fairly, that some goods spoil, and that heavy goods are hard to carry.

questions.question: Explain how money makes trade easier, using an example.
questions.expected_answer: With money, trade happens in two steps: you sell your goods for money to anyone who wants them, then use the money to buy what you need from someone else. For example, Thabo sells his oranges and uses the money to buy a pencil. Money is easy to carry, easy to divide, does not rot, can be saved and gives every item a price.
